habit.lifeForm.value: evergreen woody climber, clinging by rootlets, with a climbing juvenile phase and a bushy, flowering adult phase
habit.lifeForm.basis: RHS plant record: "a vigorous, self-clinging evergreen climber"; "mature plants produce bushy, non-clinging branches". Metcalfe 2005: "Only the vertical stems bear reproductive shoots, which are physiologically adult".

stem.maxLengthM.basis: Metcalfe 2005 (Biological Flora of the British Isles): "Climbing, sometimes reaching 30 m". The RHS gives the same figure. Not a size a ten-year-old plant has.

stem.maxDiameterM.basis: Metcalfe 2005: "Woody stems up to 25 cm diameter". The thickest stems of very old plants.

stem.youngShootColour.basis: Virginia Tech dendrology factsheet, twig: "Slender, light green but later turning light brown with aerial rootlets". An American description of the same species; no British flora read describes the colour of the shoot.

stem.youngShootHairs.value: stellate to peltate hairs, grey-white on new shoot tips
stem.youngShootHairs.basis: Metcalfe 2005: "young twigs pubescent with stellate to peltate hairs"; "Stellate trichomes on new shoot tips give a grey-white pubescent effect that diminishes as laminar growth separates them".

stem.barkOld.value: light brown, slightly rough and finely scaly, with shallow ridges and furrows on old stems
stem.barkOld.basis: Virginia Tech dendrology factsheet, bark: "Light brown slightly rough and finely scaly with numerous rootlets at the nodes". University of Connecticut plant database: on old plants light brown "with shallow ridges and furrows".

stem.rootletLengthM.basis: Melzer et al. 2010, J. R. Soc. Interface 7: unbranched attachment roots "1-15 mm long". The growth model's appendages.aerialRootLengthM is the same range.

stem.rootletsPerCluster.basis: Melzer et al. 2012, J. Exp. Bot. 63: a median of 38 roots to a root cluster (interquartile range 24, n = 191).

stem.rootletRows.basis: Melzer et al. 2012: shoots on mortar and on tree bark usually had two rows of attachment roots (up to five on cork).

stem.rootletPlace.value: unbranched, on the side of the shoot that faces what it climbs
stem.rootletPlace.basis: Melzer et al. 2012: "unbranched adventitious roots at the substrate-facing side of its shoots". Metcalfe 2005: it is the juvenile phase that produces them; adult shoots have none (Bean: bushy branches "with no aerial roots").

leaf.arrangementJuvenile.basis: Metcalfe 2005: "Juvenile plants or parts of plants bear alternately arranged, palmately lobed shade-leaves".

leaf.arrangementAdult.basis: Metcalfe 2005: reproductive shoots "bear large, spirally arranged, radially symmetrical ovate leaves". Stein and Fosket 1969 (as tabulated by the US Forest Service review): a 2/5 spiral. The engine sets the leaves of a side shoot alternately to left and right, so this cannot be drawn.

leaf.texture.basis: Metcalfe 2005: leaves "coriaceous, glabrous, evergreen"; "Leaves shining, dark green above".

leaf.colourAbove.basis: Metcalfe 2005: "Leaves shining, dark green above, often with pale veins, paler green below". Bean: "very dark glossy green".

leaf.veinColour.basis: Metcalfe 2005: "often with pale veins". RHS plant record: "often with pale green veins".

leaf.colourBeneath.basis: Metcalfe 2005: "paler green below". The viewer draws both faces of a leaf in one colour, so this is recorded and not drawn.

leaf.winterTint.basis: Metcalfe 2005: "upper surface sometimes tinged with purple in winter"; anthocyanins develop in autumn "as leaves take on their red/purple tints, and decline in spring". RHS: autumn leaves "can take on reddish or bronze tones". The engine gives an evergreen leaf no autumn or winter state, so this is recorded and not drawn.

leaf.youngColour.basis: The colour the drawing gives a leaf while it unfolds. New ivy leaves are a lighter green than old ones, as in any photograph of spring growth; no source read states it.

leaf.lifespanYears.basis: Metcalfe 2005, section VII: "Leaves are long-lived (3-4 years)".

leaf.juvenile.lobeCount.basis: Metcalfe 2005: leaves of climbing or creeping stems "palmately lobed with 3-5 triangular, entire lobes".

leaf.juvenile.lobeShape.basis: Metcalfe 2005: "3-5 triangular, entire lobes". Bean: "three or five lobes, cut either deeply or shallowly".

leaf.juvenile.outlineSideLobeReach.basis: Distance from where the stalk joins to the tip of a side lobe, as a share of the same distance to the tip of the end lobe, measured off photographs of single leaves: 0.73-0.75 (Commons: Hedera helix 2.jpg), 0.83-0.85 (Klimopblad Hedera helix.jpg), about 0.84 (Blad van klimop (Hedera helix) 02.JPG). The end lobe is the largest. No flora gives the ratio.

leaf.juvenile.outlineSideLobeBearingDeg.basis: Angle between the main vein of the end lobe and that of a side lobe, at the stalk, measured off the same photographs: 69-76 degrees (Hedera helix 2.jpg), 58-67 (Klimopblad Hedera helix.jpg), about 58 (Blad van klimop (Hedera helix) 02.JPG).

leaf.juvenile.outlineSinusDepth.basis: Distance from the stalk to the sinus between end and side lobe, as a share of the end lobe: 0.49 (Hedera helix 2.jpg), 0.55-0.58 (Klimopblad Hedera helix.jpg), about 0.68 (Blad van klimop (Hedera helix) 02.JPG): the lobes are cut a half to a third of the way in.

leaf.juvenile.outlineBasalLobes.value: small, about 0.44-0.5 of the end lobe, or merged into a rounded shoulder; a heart-shaped notch at the stalk
leaf.juvenile.outlineBasalLobes.basis: Read from the photographed leaves: the two single leaves are three-lobed, their lower margin a rounded shoulder reaching 0.46-0.53 of the end lobe behind the stalk (Hedera helix 2.jpg; Klimopblad Hedera helix.jpg); leaves on a wall include five-lobed ones whose basal lobes are small (20150318-stare-drzewce-park-hedera-helix.jpg). Metcalfe 2005: 3-5 lobes. Three of the five drawn leaves have three lobes.

leaf.juvenile.secondaryVeinAngleDeg.basis: Angle at which the pale secondary veins leave a lobe's main vein, forwards: about 40 to 50 degrees in photographs of the upper surface (Commons: Efeublatt 06.jpg; Ivy leaf (50844400051).jpg; Hedera helix 2.jpg). Not measured in any flora read.

leaf.juvenile.secondaryVeinSpacing.basis: Spacing of the secondary veins along a main vein, as a share of the end lobe's length: some six or seven a side on the end lobe in Efeublatt 06.jpg (Commons). They join into a fine pale net, which is not drawn.

leaf.juvenile.posture.value: blade hanging tip down from the end of a long stalk, upper side facing out, leaves overlapping like tiles on a wall
leaf.juvenile.posture.basis: Read from photographs of ivy on a wall and on bark (Commons: 20150318-stare-drzewce-park-hedera-helix.jpg; Atlas roslin pl Bluszcz pospolity 3368 7113.jpg, where on a trunk the blades lie flat against the bark). The drawing hangs the blade 66 to 72 degrees from the line of its stalk; which way the stalk points is the render data's.

leaf.juvenile.bladeLengthM.basis: Metcalfe 2005: leaves of climbing or creeping stems "4-10(-25) cm". The usual range; the exceptional 25 cm is left out.

leaf.juvenile.bladeWidthM.basis: VicFlora (Flora of Victoria), leaves of non-flowering shoots: 4-12 cm long, 4-7 cm wide. Naturalised plants of the same species; no British flora read gives the width.

leaf.juvenile.petioleLengthM.basis: VicFlora, leaves of non-flowering shoots: petiole 2-10(-13) cm.

leaf.adult.shape.basis: Metcalfe 2005: "leaves of flowering stems 6-10 cm, entire, ovate or rhombic". RHS: "diamond-shaped leaves".

leaf.adult.margin.basis: Bean (Trees and Shrubs Online): leaves of flowering shoots never lobed, the margins wavy or entire, more narrowly ovate.

leaf.adult.petioleLengthM.basis: VicFlora, leaves of flowering shoots: petioles 2.5-11 cm long.

inflorescence.type.basis: Metcalfe 2005: flowers "c. 20 in terminal globose umbels, which may be arranged into panicles". Bean: "a terminal cluster of globose umbels".

inflorescence.umbelsPerPanicle.basis: Metcalfe 2005, section VII: "3-5 umbels in a panicle". Elsewhere in the same account, "panicles of 1-6 umbels": the wider range is not drawn.

inflorescence.flowersPerUmbel.basis: Metcalfe 2005: "There are about 20 flowers in each umbel".

inflorescence.flowersPerUmbelRange.basis: US Forest Service review (Fire Effects Information System): each umbel has 8 (Vezza et al. 2006) to 20 (Metcalfe 2005) flowers. The lower umbels of a panicle are drawn with fewer flowers than the end one, within this range; which umbel has fewer is not stated by either.

inflorescence.umbelDiameterM.basis: An online flora of Crete, for subsp. helix: flowers "in 3-5 cm diam. umbels". The only measurement of the umbel found; neither Metcalfe nor Bean gives one.

inflorescence.extentM.basis: The greatest extent of the whole panicle, which is what the growth model's organs.racemeLengthM measures and what the drawing is scaled to. Derived from 3 to 5 umbels of 3 to 5 cm, the end one above the others; no source read measures the panicle.

inflorescence.openingOrder.value: the end umbel first, then the others in turn back towards the leaves; the flowers of one umbel more or less together
inflorescence.openingOrder.basis: Metcalfe 2005: "the terminal umbel flowering first, followed by successive umbels back to the leafy growth"; "flowers in an umbel open more or less synchronously".

inflorescence.indumentum.value: stalks and receptacle felted with stellate hairs
inflorescence.indumentum.basis: Metcalfe 2005: "Peduncle, pedicels and receptacle stellate-tomentose". Drawn as a grey cast on the stalks.

flower.petalColour.basis: Metcalfe 2005: petals "yellowish-green". Bean: flowers "yellowish green". RHS: "greenish-yellow".

flower.petalShape.value: triangular-ovate, hooded at the tip, free
flower.petalShape.basis: Metcalfe 2005: "triangular-ovate, somewhat hooded at apex; free".

flower.petalPosture.basis: How the drawing holds the petals of an open flower. Not stated in the floras read; open ivy flowers show the petals turned back below the disc.

flower.antherColour.basis: Metcalfe 2005: "The anthers are bright yellow, turning brownish-yellow and falling off quickly (1-3 days) after anthesis".

flower.discColour.basis: Konarska 2014, Acta Sci. Pol. Hortorum Cultus 13: the nectary disc on top of the ovary is green when it begins to secrete and gradually turns brown. Metcalfe 2005: "a domed disk surrounding the styles", which glistens with nectar. One colour between the two is drawn.

flower.discDiameterM.basis: Konarska 2014, table 1: "Length of nectary (mm) 2.1 +/- 0.3" (n = 10), read here as the width of the disc across the top of the ovary.

flower.ovaryTopDiameterM.basis: Width of the top of the inferior ovary, round the nectar disc, of an open flower: about 3 mm, read from photographs in which flowers and berries can be set against one another (Commons: Gemeiner Efeu (Bahnhofstrasse, Neuendettelsau) 20250911 143302.jpg; Hedera helix 002.JPG, H. Zell). Wider than the disc itself (flower.discDiameterM, 2.1 mm, Konarska 2014) and short of the 6-8 mm berry it swells into. No source read measures it. The first pass drew it 2.5 mm, which left the umbel looking sparse beside the photographs.

flower.styleLengthM.basis: VicFlora: style about 1.5 mm long, stout, united, persistent. Metcalfe 2005: "styles joined into a column".

flower.lifeDays.basis: Konarska 2014: ivy flowers "live for about a week". Metcalfe 2005: the stamens fall about 7 days after anthesis.

fruit.diameterM.basis: Metcalfe 2005: "globose, 6-8 mm"; measured fruits 5.5-7.5 x 5.5-8.7 mm. Bean: about 1/4 in. across.

fruit.colourRipe.basis: Metcalfe 2005: "bluish- or greenish-black (rarely yellow or white)"; "a purple-black berry". Bean: "dull inky black".

fruit.colourUnripe.basis: The colour the drawing gives a berry before it ripens. Unripe ivy berries are green, as in photographs of ivy in early winter; the descriptions read give only the ripe colour.

fruit.seedCount.basis: Metcalfe 2005: "seeds 1-5". Not drawn: the seeds are inside the berry.

fruit.crown.value: the style persists as a short point in the middle of the flat top of the berry
fruit.crown.basis: VicFlora: style about 1.5 mm long, stout, united, persistent. The disc round it stays as the flat top of the berry.

fruit.umbelsFruitingPerPanicle.basis: Metcalfe 2005: "Typically only one umbel per panicle develops into fruit, normally the terminal one". One fruit record is therefore one umbel of berries.

fruit.berriesPerUmbel.basis: How many berries the drawing gives a fruiting umbel. No count was found in a flora. In photographs a ripe umbel shows some fifteen berries on its visible side, crowded and touching (Commons: 2026-04-11 Hedera helix im NSG Jockgrimer Tongruben, Achim Lammerts), and a few flowers of most umbels set nothing and leave bare stalks (20151224Hedera helix1.jpg). The first pass drew 10 to 18, spaced apart.

fruit.clusterWidthM.basis: The width of the fruiting umbel, which is what the growth model's fruit.lengthM measures and what the drawing is scaled to. No source read measures the cluster. Read from photographs: a ripe umbel is a tight ball some four berries of 6 to 8 mm across (Metcalfe 2005), about 2.5 to 3.5 cm (Commons: 2026-04-11 Hedera helix im NSG Jockgrimer Tongruben, Achim Lammerts). The first pass took 3 to 4 cm from the umbel in flower, which spread the berries apart.

fruit.colourRipening.value: green, then dull purple-brown, then blue-black
fruit.colourRipening.basis: Read from photographs of ivy in December, in which half-grown berries are purplish brown beside green ones (Commons: 20151224Hedera helix1.jpg). The drawing's ripe colour is a purple-black so that a berry part way through ripening passes through a dull purple and not an olive.
